justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are fulfilled: Video Streaming Service handles R-01, Prescription Engine and Integration Service cover R-02, AI Symptom Checker Service provides R-03 triage, and Consent & Policy Enforcement Engine with Local Consent & State Manager satisfy R-04.
justifications.performance_efficiency: High efficiency is achieved via Caching Layer (Redis), mediasoup SFU Router Core, local ONNX Runtime inference, Pub/Sub asynchronous event ingestion, and PgBouncer connection pooling to support high throughput and minimal latency.
justifications.compatibility: Explicitly satisfies R-08 via the Integration Service, featuring the FHIR Adapter Component for US HL7 FHIR standards, EU E-Prescription Gateway Component, and Transformation Engine Component for European national formats.
justifications.usability: Web & Mobile Apps serves both Patients and Clinicians with offline support via Offline Data Synchronizer. However, clinician workflows and dedicated audit/administrative interfaces are combined into broad presentation components without role-specific UX specialization.
justifications.reliability: Reliability under adverse conditions (R-06) is thoroughly handled by Adaptive Bitrate & Quality Manager, Degraded Mode Handler, TURN/STUN Relay Manager for NAT traversal, and BullMQ Retry & Dead-Letter Queue Component for outbound requests.
justifications.security: Strictly enforces GDPR and HIPAA through Data Residency Enforcer Component, OPA Authorization Engine, federated mTLS between gateways, Data Masking & Tokenization Component, Google Cloud KMS encryption, and BigQuery immutability for MDR traceability.
justifications.maintainability: Strong modularity with decoupled containers and cohesive components. Responsibilities such as transformation (Transformation Engine Component), policy enforcement (OPA), and clinical triage (Clinical Triage Validator) are cleanly separated, minimizing coupling and easing testing.
justifications.portability: Targets europe-west3 and us-central1 accurately using standard runtimes (Go, Node.js, Python). However, components are tightly coupled to GCP proprietary services like Google Cloud API Gateway, BigQuery, and Pub/Sub, limiting cloud provider portability.

PERF-01.justification: Mediasoup SFU router core and signaling server handle video routing with adaptive bitrates, supported by Redis caching and connection pooling, though explicit horizontal autoscaling policies for SFU nodes are not fully elaborated.
sensitivity_points: mediasoup SFU CPU utilization and egress bandwidth limits under high load
tradeoffs: SFU server density per host versus video routing latency and packet loss

PERF-02.justification: FastAPI with local ONNX Runtime enables rapid local quantized inference, while non-blocking asynchronous audit logging via Google Cloud Pub/Sub easily satisfies the ~14 requests/second load within the 3-second threshold.
sensitivity_points: ONNX Runtime inference execution latency and Pub/Sub publishing throughput
tradeoffs: Model quantization level versus triage output accuracy and inference speed

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture explicitly features an Adaptive Bitrate & Quality Manager (<300 kbit/s simulcast layer adaptation), Degraded Mode Handler, and client-side Offline Data Synchronizer to maintain audio/calls and preserve clinical notes.
sensitivity_points: Bandwidth degradation detection latency and simulcast layer switching threshold
tradeoffs: Sacrificing video resolution to preserve essential audio fidelity and session continuity

AVAIL-02.justification: The architecture deploys only to us-central1 and europe-west3 with strict residency rules; without a secondary US region or automated multi-region disaster recovery within the US, service cannot be restored within one hour.
elements: Google Cloud API Gateway with OPA
sensitivity_points: Recovery point objective and cross-zone replication speed within the single US region
tradeoffs: Cost efficiency of single-region US deployment versus rapid disaster recovery capability

MOD-01.justification: The Integration Service decouples national variations using a dedicated EU E-Prescription Gateway and Transformation Engine, confining country-specific mapping adjustments to templates without impacting core telehealth or persistence logic.
sensitivity_points: Flexibility and expressiveness of template engine mappings across national standards
tradeoffs: Generic transformation engine maintainability versus type safety of bespoke code adapters

MOD-02.justification: Symptom Checker Orchestrator and ML Model Runtime handle model execution, and Audit & Traceability Logger immutably stores model versions and inputs in BigQuery, though hot runtime rollbacks lack explicit orchestration mechanisms.
sensitivity_points: Consistent propagation of model version metadata through triage pipelines
tradeoffs: Fine-grained version traceability logging versus storage footprint in BigQuery

SEC-01.justification: Federated mTLS gateways require authorization by Open Policy Agent and the Core Telehealth Consent Engine, blocking cross-region data transfers without explicit patient consent and recording access attempts in audit logs.
elements: Google Cloud API Gateway with OPA
sensitivity_points: Correctness of OPA Rego policies evaluating cross-border clinician access context
tradeoffs: Synchronous authorization policy evaluation latency versus strict data residency compliance

SEC-02.justification: Consent updates are processed by the Consent & Policy Enforcement Engine and OPA dynamically at request time, while CDC pipelines and BigQuery ensure rapid cache invalidation and verifiable audit trails well under 24 hours.
sensitivity_points: Cache TTL and invalidation latency across Redis and API Gateway layers
tradeoffs: Immediate cache invalidation overhead versus real-time consent enforcement accuracy
